title: What If Every Undersea Internet Cable Was Cut?

scenes.text: What if every undersea cable was cut? About ninety-nine percent of overseas internet rides through them.
Hundreds of thousands of miles of fiber-optic cable lie on the ocean floor.
Tonga shows the effect. In January 2022 a volcano damaged its only cable, and about one hundred and five thousand people were almost entirely cut off.
Repairs were expected to take at least four weeks. An earlier cut in 2019 took nearly two weeks to fix.
Cables do break. A 2006 earthquake near Taiwan disrupted eight of them at once.
One researcher estimates that cutting the cluster of cables off Egypt could shut down a third of the global internet.

description:
What if every undersea internet cable was cut?
About 99 percent of transoceanic data travels through them, and Tonga was nearly cut off for weeks when its only cable broke.
